about: The golden set of the letter checks (#78): invented people, postings and letter sentences, each labelled with what the checks must say. Run before a change to a prompt or to a claim rule ships: tests/test_letter_evals.py. Add a case for every false alarm or missed claim found; never change a label to make a run pass. The inv-* cases were written before the #109 rules, but many of their sentences are also development rows in tests/test_claims.py, so their recall is a development number, not a held-out one; a fresh held-out batch should come from another writer. A case with "gap" is a known miss: it keeps its true label and runs as a strict expected failure, so a fix shows at once. The h113-* cases (#113) are held-out: another writer wrote them before the #113 code, and they must never be copied into tests/test_claims.py. The wording of some h113-* cases was seen during development, so their recall counts as development, not held-out: exact copies h113-1n-dev-course, h113-4-dev-present-labs, h113-6-acc-fluent; near copies h113-1n-dev-reviewed-posting, h113-1n-care-course, h113-2n-dev-new-subject, h113-4n-dev-tool-for-slack, h113-4n-acc-macro-for-excel, h113-5n-dev-python-version, h113-6-dev-native-speaker, h113-6n-dev-company, h113-6n-acc-fluent-excel. The h113r-* cases (#113, fix round) are hard negatives and true positives written after the first #113 code, for past-participle openings, requirement wording and the English exemption.
